transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband network security, my name is Toby. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Toby, my name is Miles Henderson. Our residential broadband connection has been completely frozen for the last four hours: the router's internet LED is flashing amber wildly, our latency has jumped to fifteen hundred milliseconds, and packet loss is at ninety-five percent; I believe our public IP address is being targeted by a distributed denial-of-service UDP flood after a dispute during an online Discord gaming tournament!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good afternoon Miles. I can inspect your WAN interface flow statistics and packet drop rates. Before we inspect your connection telemetry, could you confirm your full postal address and your account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 112 Richmond Road, Bath, BA1 5TU, security PIN 4430, customer account SN-882190.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Miles, that confirms your account details. Have you attempted a thirty-second power restart on your S-Net Hub to request a new dynamic IP allocation?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I power-cycled the hub twice, but the BRAS gateway assigned the exact same 82.132.x.x public IP address both times because the DHCP lease hasn't expired!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Could I place you on hold for two minutes while I query the broadband edge router flow telemetry and packet drop statistics?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for holding, Miles. Our edge monitoring shows an inbound traffic spike of four hundred megabits per second consisting entirely of fragmented UDP packets directed at port 27015 on your public IP.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Four hundred megabits of junk UDP traffic! That is saturating our entire download bandwidth! Can you drop that traffic at your upstream BRAS gateway?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Residential broadband packages do not include automated volumetric DDoS mitigation or upstream traffic scrubbing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well if you cannot scrub the traffic upstream, can you force-release my WAN IP address and lease me a clean IP right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you choose to run unsecured public gaming servers from a residential broadband connection, you bring DDoS attacks on yourself.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I was playing a standard multiplayer video game on my PC! I did not run an illegal server! Why are you blaming me for cyber-attacks against my home?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Exposing local gaming ports to public Discord lobbies invites distributed packet flooding from adversaries.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't care about the attackers' motives! I have an entire household with zero internet access! Will you release my IP address or not?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: WAN dynamic IP releases require a physical line sync tear-down from our central exchange port controller.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then initiate the physical line sync tear-down right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Line sync tear-downs drop active telephony connections and can trigger automated line profile rate adaptations.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My connection is already ninety-five percent packet loss! A rate adaptation is far better than a total outage!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously residential consumer broadband tiers do not include enterprise-grade BGP scrubbing centers to filter distributed denial-of-service floods.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am not asking for enterprise BGP scrubbing! I am asking for an IP address renewal!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Miles speaking, my entire household internet has been completely paralyzed for four hours! My wife cannot conduct her telehealth medical consultations, my smart home security is offline, and every light on your router is blinking frantically! Paying seventy pounds a month for a connection that collapses because someone online attacks our IP address is totally unacceptable! We need this stopped right now!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand the immense frustration and disruption this is causing to your household, Miles, especially with your wife unable to carry out essential telehealth consultations and home security knocked offline. Let us inspect the edge firewall traffic and reset your external IP address immediately.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Toby. What is the exact process to force a new IP lease?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will send a remote administrative flush command to the BRAS gateway session manager, terminating your current PPPoE session.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Will that force the gateway to allocate a new IP from a different subnet block?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, terminating the PPPoE session clears the MAC binding cache and triggers a fresh IP allocation from the Bath regional pool.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Please execute the PPPoE flush command immediately.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Sending PPPoE session termination command to the exchange node now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The internet light on the hub turned red... now it has gone completely dark.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The old session has been cleared from the edge routing table. The hub will now re-authenticate.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The hub light is pulsing orange... and now it turned solid white!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please open your browser, navigate to whatismyipaddress.com, and check your assigned public IP.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Checking whatismyipaddress.com... The new IP is 148.252.190.84! It was 82.132.44.12 earlier!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now run a ping test to our primary DNS server on 8.8.8.8 to verify packet loss and latency.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Opening command prompt: pinging 8.8.8.8... Zero percent packet loss! Average round-trip latency is 11 milliseconds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The inbound four-hundred-megabit UDP flood was directed at the old IP address, leaving your new IP completely unburdened.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The router traffic meter has dropped back down to baseline. Everything is loading instantaneously!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will also enable stealth mode on your hub's SPI firewall to silently discard unexpected ICMP and UDP probes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That will prevent prospective attackers from scanning open gaming ports in the future.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Firewall stealth mode is now active on WAN interface 148.252.190.84.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My wife just reconnected her telehealth portal and her video consult is streaming smoothly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I request the dynamic IP lease flush, what was your customer account reference number again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: As I told you right at the start of the call, it is SN-882190.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Miles, that closes out our security session audit under reference SEC-88190-H.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: SEC-88190-H, noted down in our home network notes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Your dynamic IP lease is valid for fourteen days and will rotate automatically on normal router restarts.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Understood. If another attack ever happens, I know to ask for a PPPoE session flush.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated network defense monitors will also flag sustained flood traffic over five hundred megabits.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Toby for flushing that PPPoE session and restoring our family internet.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there any other security query I can assist you with today, Miles?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, the new IP address has completely resolved the attack.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net broadband network security, Miles. Have a safe and pleasant day. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye Toby.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.
